arXiv:1409.5174v2 [math.AP] 28 Sep 2015

On the three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics system in scaling-invariant spaces

Kazuo Yamazaki
Abstract.

We study the criterion for the velocity and magnetic vector fields that solve the three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics system, given any initial data sufficiently smooth, to experience a finite-time blowup. Following the work of [12] and making use of the structure of the system, we obtain a criterion that is imposed on the magnetic vector field and only one of the three components of the velocity vector field, both in scaling-invariant spaces.

Keywords: Navier-Stokes equations, Magnetohydrodynamics system, global regularity, anisotropic Littlewood-Paley theory.

11 1 2000MSC : 35B65, 35Q35, 35Q8622 2 Department of Mathematics, Washington State University, Pullman, WA 99164-3113, USA

1. Introduction and statement of results

We study the following magnetohydrodynamics system in ℝ3\mathbb{R}^{3}:

where u,b:ℝ3×ℝ+↦ℝ3u,b:\mathbb{R}^{3}\times\mathbb{R}^{+}\mapsto\mathbb{R}^{3} represent the velocity and magnetic vector fields respectively while π:ℝ3×ℝ+↦ℝ\pi:\mathbb{R}^{3}\times\mathbb{R}^{+}\mapsto\mathbb{R} the scalar pressure field, ν≥0\nu\geq 0 the viscosity and η≥0\eta\geq 0 the magnetic diffusivity. Without loss of generality, hereafter we assume ν=η=1\nu=\eta=1 and also write ∂t\partial_{t} for dd​t\frac{d}{dt} and ∂i\partial_{i} for dd​xi,i=1,2,3,x=(x1,x2,x3)\frac{d}{dx_{i}},i=1,2,3,x=(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}). Let us also set for any three-dimensional vector field f=(f1,f2,f3),fh≜(f1,f2,0)f=(f^{1},f^{2},f^{3}),f^{h}\triangleq(f^{1},f^{2},0),

Ω≜∇×u,j≜∇×b,ω≜Ω⋅e3,d≜j⋅e3​ where ​e3≜(0,0,1).\Omega\triangleq\nabla\times u,\hskip 14.22636ptj\triangleq\nabla\times b,\hskip 14.22636pt\omega\triangleq\Omega\cdot e^{3},\hskip 14.22636ptd\triangleq j\cdot e^{3}\hskip 2.84526pt\text{ where }e^{3}\triangleq(0,0,1).

When b≡0b\equiv 0, (1a)-(1c) recovers the Navier-Stokes equations (NSE), for which the question of whether a smooth local solution can preserve its regularity for all time remains unknown. The analogous problem for the MHD system (1a)-(1c) remains just as difficult, if not more. One of the sources of the difficulty of the global regularity issue of the MHD system (1a)-(1c) may be traced back to the rescaling and its known bounded quantities. It can be shown that if (u,b)​(x,t)(u,b)(x,t) solves the system (1a)-(1c), then so does (uλ,bλ)​(x,t)≜λ⁡(u,b)​(λ​x,λ2​t)(u_{\lambda},b_{\lambda})(x,t)\triangleq\lambda(u,b)(\lambda x,\lambda^{2}t) while ∥uλ​(x,t)∥L22+∥bλ​(x,t)∥L22=λ−1​(∥u⁡(x,λ2​t)∥L22+∥b⁡(x,λ2​t)∥L22)\lVert u_{\lambda}(x,t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert b_{\lambda}(x,t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}=\lambda^{-1}(\lVert u(x,\lambda^{2}t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert b(x,\lambda^{2}t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}).

In two-dimensional case, both the NSE and the MHD system, if ν,η>0\nu,\eta>0, admit a unique global smooth solution starting from any data sufficiently smooth (cf. [22, 24]). Due to the difficulty in the three-dimensional case, much effort has been devoted to provide regularity and blow-up criterion some of which we review now.

In [25], the author initiated important research direction of regularity criterion which led to, along with others such as [13], that if a weak solution uu of the three-dimensional NSE with ν>0\nu>0 satisfies

u∈Lr​(0,T,Lp​(ℝ3)),3p+2r≤1,p∈[3,∞],u\in L^{r}(0,T;L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{3})),\hskip 8.53581pt\frac{3}{p}+\frac{2}{r}\leq 1,p\in[3,\infty],

then uu is smooth. Among many other results, in [3] it was shown that if uu solves the NSE with ν>0\nu>0 and

∇u∈Lr​(0,T,Lp​(ℝ3)),3p+2r≤2,1<r≤3,\nabla u\in L^{r}(0,T;L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{3})),\hskip 8.53581pt\frac{3}{p}+\frac{2}{r}\leq 2,\hskip 8.53581pt1<r\leq 3,

then uu is a regular solution (cf. also [2, 15]). We emphasize that the norm ∥⋅∥LTr​Lxp\lVert\cdot\rVert_{L_{T}^{r}L_{x}^{p}} and ∥⋅∥LTr​W˙x1,p\lVert\cdot\rVert_{L_{T}^{r}\dot{W}_{x}^{1,p}} are both invariant under the scalings of the solutions to the NSE and the MHD system precisely when 3p+2r=1,3p+2r=2\frac{3}{p}+\frac{2}{r}=1,\frac{3}{p}+\frac{2}{r}=2 respectively. For the MHD system, e.g. the author in [26] showed that if ∇u,∇b∈L4​(0,T,L2​(ℝ3)),\nabla u,\nabla b\in L^{4}(0,T;L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{3})), then no singularity occurs in [0,T][0,T]. Moreover, the work in [6] in particular showed that if [0,T∗)[0,T^{\ast}) is the maximal interval of existence of smooth solution and T∗<∞T^{\ast}<\infty, then

∫0T∗∥Ω∥L∞+∥j∥L∞​𝑑τ=∞.\int_{0}^{T^{\ast}}\lVert\Omega\rVert_{L^{\infty}}+\lVert j\rVert_{L^{\infty}}d\tau=\infty.

We note that the authors in [16, 36] independently realized that in particular the criterion for the solution to the MHD system may be reduced to just uu, dropping condition on bb completely (see also [17, 27]). Let us also state results that are directly related to our work. In [14] the authors showed that given u0∈H˙12​(ℝ3)u_{0}\in\dot{H}^{\frac{1}{2}}(\mathbb{R}^{3}), there exists a maximal interval [0,T∗)[0,T^{\ast}) on which a unique solution uu to the NSE exists. Analogous results with (u0,b0)∈H˙12​(ℝ3)(u_{0},b_{0})\in\dot{H}^{\frac{1}{2}}(\mathbb{R}^{3}) may be found in [23, 35].

We now survey some component reduction results of such conditions. The authors in [21] showed that if uu solves the NSE with ν>0\nu>0 and

u3∈\displaystyle u^{3}\in Lr​(0,T,Lp​(ℝ3)),3p+2r≤58,r∈[5423,185],\displaystyle L^{r}(0,T;L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{3})),\hskip 2.84526pt\frac{3}{p}+\frac{2}{r}\leq\frac{5}{8},\hskip 14.22636ptr\in[\frac{54}{23},\frac{18}{5}],
or ∇u3∈\displaystyle\text{ or }\nabla u^{3}\in Lr​(0,T,Lp​(ℝ3)),3p+2r≤116,r∈[245,∞],\displaystyle L^{r}(0,T;L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{3})),\hskip 2.84526pt\frac{3}{p}+\frac{2}{r}\leq\frac{11}{6},\hskip 8.53581ptr\in[\frac{24}{5},\infty],

then the solution is regular (see also [7 , 37] for similar results on u3,∇u3u^{3},\nabla u^{3}). This result was successfully extended to the MHD system as the authors in [20] showed that if uu solves (1a)-(1c) with ν,η>0\nu,\eta>0 and

u3,b∈Lr​(0,T,Lp​(ℝ3)),3p+2r≤34+12​p,p>103,u^{3},b\in L^{r}(0,T;L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{3})),\hskip 8.53581pt\frac{3}{p}+\frac{2}{r}\leq\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{2p},\hskip 8.53581ptp>\frac{10}{3}, (2)

then the solution pair (u,b)(u,b) remains smooth for all time. In [32], the author reduced this constraint on u3,bu^{3},b to u3,b1,b2u^{3},b^{1},b^{2} in special cases without worsening the upper bound of 34+12​p\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{2p} making use of the structure of (1b). We note however that the upper bound of 34+12​p\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{2p} does not allow the norm to be scaling-invariant. For more interesting component reduction results of such criterion, we refer to e.g. [8, 9, 30, 31]. In particular, we point out that the author in [33] obtained the following regularity criterion for the solution to the three-dimensional MHD system:

{u3∈Lr1(0,T;Lp1(ℝ3)),3p1+2r1≤13+12​p1,152<p1,d∈Lr2(0,T;Lp2(ℝ3)),3p2+2r2≤2,32<p2.\begin{cases}u^{3}\in L^{r_{1}}(0,T;L^{p_{1}}(\mathbb{R}^{3})),\hskip 14.22636pt\frac{3}{p_{1}}+\frac{2}{r_{1}}\leq\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{2p_{1}},\hskip 2.84526pt\frac{15}{2}<p_{1},\\ d\in L^{r_{2}}(0,T;L^{p_{2}}(\mathbb{R}^{3})),\hskip 19.91692pt\frac{3}{p_{2}}+\frac{2}{r_{2}}\leq 2,\hskip 34.1433pt\frac{3}{2}<p_{2}.\end{cases} (3)

We remark that the upper bound of p2,r2p_{2},r_{2} for dd allows the scaling-invariant case.

We now motivate our study. In [12], the authors succeeded in showing that given an initial data for the NSE in W˙1,32​(ℝ3)\dot{W}^{1,\frac{3}{2}}(\mathbb{R}^{3}), if blow-up occurs at T∗<∞T^{\ast}<\infty, then u3∉Lp​(0,T∗,H˙12+2p),p∈(4,6)u_{3}\notin L^{p}(0,T^{\ast};\dot{H}^{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{p}}),p\in(4,6). The purpose of this manuscript is to extend this result to the MHD system (1a)-(1c). We emphasize that because the proof in [12] required taking a curl of the NSE and studying its vorticity formulation carefully, such a generalization to the MHD system is non-trivial. A well-known example for this type of difficulty is that although in two-dimensional case, the author in [34] showed that the solution to the Euler equations admits a unique global smooth solution, it remains unknown if such a result may be extended to the two-dimensional MHD system even with full magnetic diffusion (see [10] and references found therein). Similarly, although in [11], the authors obtained a two-vorticity component regularity criterion for the three-dimensional NSE making use of the Biot-Savart law in a special way, to the best of the author’s knowledge, an analogous criterion, e.g. in terms of two-vorticity components, does not exist for the MHD system. The difficulty in extending these results is due to the current density formulation upon taking a curl on (1b) (in particular M⁡(u,b)M(u,b) in (19)). This difficulty appears even in two-dimensional case, e.g. [18] in which the author elaborates why the current density formulation is not as simple as that of vorticity.

Remark 1.1.
  1. (1)

    In comparison with (2) and (3), the conditions in (4) is at the scaling-invariant level.

  2. (2)

    Taking b≡0b\equiv 0 recovers the result in [12].

The difficulty in the estimate of the third component of the velocity equation is the pressure term which now involves the quadratic of the magnetic field (see (41a)). We had to take advantage of the structure of the MHD system, in particular make cancellations such as in (21)-(23) (see also (43a)-(43e)) and (V1+V​I1)1(V_{1}+VI_{1})_{1} and (V1+V​I1)4(V_{1}+VI_{1})_{4} in (82).

In the Preliminaries we set up notations and state key lemmas. Thereafter, we prove the second statement of Theorem 1.1, namely (4). Because local existence theory is classical, we sketch it in the Appendix for completeness.

Here we prove two additional estimates:

∥f​g∥H˙s−1,σ1+σ2−12≲∥f∥(B˙2,11)h​(B˙2,1σ1)v​∥g∥H˙s−1,σ2,\displaystyle\lVert fg\rVert_{\dot{H}^{s-1,\sigma_{1}+\sigma_{2}-\frac{1}{2}}}\lesssim\lVert f\rVert_{(\dot{B}_{2,1}^{1})_{h}(\dot{B}_{2,1}^{\sigma_{1}})_{v}}\lVert g\rVert_{\dot{H}^{s-1,\sigma_{2}}}, (94)
